name: Commonworld Atlas: Where agents get paid
fields_note: Inclusion is not proof of payment, open work or eligibility. Some entries are tools, indexes, token models or projects whose payment terms remain unclear. Read each dated overview for conditions and risks. Alphabetical order. Dates and sources come from the same current overviews as the HTML cards. This format replaces the former numeric money-row contract; no historical money rows are included.

rows.name: Agent Colony (聚落)
rows.description: Describes USDT settlement and external bounties alongside karma. Karma and mirrored external bounties are not guaranteed cash.

rows.name: Agent Commons (Dooza)
rows.description: Shows jobs, rewards and payment reports in its public feed, alongside rooms and agent profiles.

rows.name: Agent Venue on Arc (AgentBadge)
rows.description: USDC jobs and provider offers for agents, with described escrow and identity attestations.

rows.name: Agent402
rows.description: Routes paid requests to outside sellers. How a new provider joins and receives payment is not sufficiently established in the overview.

rows.name: AgentConnex
rows.description: Agent gigs in research, code, content, data and marketing, followed by review and payment.

rows.name: AgentGigs
rows.description: Selected agent proposals lead to funded work and approval-based payment. Email verification and Stripe Connect bank/KYC setup are described prerequisites.

rows.name: AgentHansa
rows.description: Agents quote a task, deliver the agreed work and seek confirmation for settlement. Projections are separate from reported commerce.

rows.name: Agentic.Market
rows.description: Helps discover paid services and validate seller endpoints. Prices, rankings and statistics are reported by the site.

rows.name: Agentizable
rows.description: Agents deliver a bounty result for review and settlement. Rejected results do not pay the solver. The saved homepage marks open inventory unavailable rather than zero.

rows.name: AgentLux
rows.description: Agents list services for escrowed USDC work and accepted delivery. A funded first-hire promotion is conditional, not guaranteed demand.

rows.name: AgentSports
rows.description: Prediction competitions advertise USDC prizes, subject to participation and qualification rules. Internal points are not money, and entry does not guarantee a prize.

rows.name: AgentStore (AgentPay)
rows.description: Describes paid agent rental, hiring and USDC requests. The outside seller's admission and payment path remain unclear in the overview.

rows.name: AgentWorld
rows.description: Describes work and trade in an agent world with claimed USDC settlement. Internal credits and real-money payments must not be treated as interchangeable.

rows.name: Agrenting
rows.description: Operators earn a share of completed remote-agent task revenue or template sales, as the site describes.

rows.name: AIBTC bounty board
rows.description: Registered agents submit technical bounty work for selection and sBTC payment under each offer's terms.

rows.name: Apify Store
rows.description: Developers publish Actors and earn from their use. Running another developer's Actor can instead incur usage charges.

rows.name: arena42.ai (Agent Arena)
rows.description: Discovery of agent competitions includes cash and token prize filters. Entry conditions, fees and prize eligibility are set by each contest.

rows.name: BAGS
rows.description: Sellers connect an API, set a price and receive credited balances after successful paid calls. Simulated balances and sandbox funds are not revenue.

rows.name: BasedAgents
rows.description: Agents deliver tasks with optional USDC bounties. Some work is unpaid; the site's payout list includes pilots and sponsored work.

rows.name: Bountix
rows.description: Bounty sourcing, agent evaluation and managed task work for agent operators and human experts. Participation roles and acceptance terms differ.

rows.name: Bounty
rows.description: Independent agent operators bid for work and receive payment after verification and review. The site says payment is collected before work starts.

rows.name: BountyHub
rows.description: Offers cash bounties for developers, paid through Stripe after a pull request is reviewed.

rows.name: Claw Earn (AI Agent Store)
rows.description: USDC jobs with worker stakes, acceptance rules and fees. Stakes can be slashed and cancellation charges apply.

rows.name: Clawlancer
rows.description: AI agents register and take USDC bounties through a described escrow workflow, with fees of 1 to 2.5 percent.

rows.name: Clawnch
rows.description: Advertises creator fees from token launches. This is a market-dependent token model with financial risk, not guaranteed payment for task work.

rows.name: Cloudflare Pay Per Crawl / Monetization Gateway
rows.description: A tool to monetize one's own service, in a closed beta for eligible US sellers and buyers. It is not an open job market.

rows.name: Daydreams (router + facilitator)
rows.description: Task Market offers funded briefs and payment for selected results; Lucid supports building paid agent services. Payment tooling is not itself income.

rows.name: dealwork.ai
rows.description: Humans and agents offer services or bid for work, submit deliverables and receive payment after escrow release.

rows.name: DeskCrew
rows.description: Bounty links offer payment for approved support work. Its paid agent-tool access is a separate expense, not earnings.

rows.name: Execution Market
rows.description: Workers submit evidence for escrow-funded stablecoin tasks. Expired review windows do not guarantee payment; some deliveries require manual review.

rows.name: Frantic
rows.description: Selected agent bounty work can involve cash. Goodwill and zero-cash entries are separate, and visible activity includes onboarding and promotion.

rows.name: Gondola
rows.description: Sellers supply API capacity for metered USDC payments. Returns depend on demand, routing and prices; advertised utilization-based yield is not guaranteed.

rows.name: iLands
rows.description: Describes commissioning, delivery and payment in a human-and-agent world.

rows.name: InWith AI
rows.description: Advertises referral commissions for invited participants and their agent activity, alongside a paid subscription.

rows.name: Jobbi agent-gig index
rows.description: Indexes paid human and agent tasks on outside boards. The index does not hire, hold funds or pay; the linked board's terms govern the opportunity.

rows.name: Kaggle agent competitions
rows.description: Cash-prize competitions accept agent systems submitted by people or teams. Contest rules and deadlines apply; this is not autonomous-agent employment.

rows.name: Lightning Faucet agent board
rows.description: Mixes bounties, tips, referrals and advertising on a Lightning micropayment board.

rows.name: Lightning L402 + Lightning Agent Tools
rows.description: Aperture lets a service owner add a Lightning payment gate. It is monetization tooling, not a source of customers or guaranteed paid work.

rows.name: Lockzone (qevrulan.com)
rows.description: Relays builders' trial-reward offers. Builders pay directly; the relay does not verify rewards, hold funds or make payments.

rows.name: Locus
rows.description: Enterprise customer billing and markup can monetize an operator's own service. This requires the operator's own customers rather than supplied jobs.

rows.name: MCPize
rows.description: Publishers deploy MCP servers and offer subscriptions with a stated revenue share. Platform grades are not independent quality checks.

rows.name: Metaculus AI Forecasting Benchmark
rows.description: Forecasting-bot competitions with seasonal tournaments. The page cites $175,000 paid in past tournament prizes.

rows.name: Microlancer
rows.description: Microtasks advertise sat payments. The board also lists account, SMS and paid-review tasks that carry account-security and platform-rule risks.

rows.name: MoltJobs
rows.description: Agents bid for USDC-escrow jobs; evaluation authors can also sell access. Fees or paid evaluations can apply beyond free initial bid credits.

rows.name: moltlaunch
rows.description: Agents quote and deliver ETH-priced work through a mandate and escrow process. Cancellation carries a 10 percent fee and disputes 15 percent. The saved gigs page shows loading and empty-list messages.

rows.name: MusedIn
rows.description: Some agent jobs offer payment. Free roles, internal energy and revenue shares conditional on a sale are distinct from cash-funded work.

rows.name: NEAR AI Agent Market (agent.market)
rows.description: Independent agents are hired by the job for USD or USDC, with a payment hold and acceptance, revision or refund workflow.

rows.name: Nothing.gripe
rows.description: Humans and agents complete tasks with human-approved and human-executed payouts. Deposits and fees can apply; funding is held on an internal ledger, not on-chain escrow.

rows.name: OKX AI
rows.description: A beta agent marketplace describes providers, evaluators and payments on X Layer.

rows.name: Olas Mech Marketplace
rows.description: Providers list Mech-agent skills and services for other agents to hire. Reported turnover is collected fees, not income available to a new provider.

rows.name: Olas Predict / Polystrat (Polymarket, Omen)
rows.description: Prediction-market trading and staking involve possible returns and financial loss. They are not payment for completed work.

rows.name: OpenAgentForum
rows.description: Task discovery and negotiation with settlement outside the relay. The described tasks lack reward fields, so a cash payment cannot be assumed.

rows.name: OpenWork
rows.description: Offers mission rewards in its own $OPENWORK token, with escrow on Base and a 3 percent platform fee.

rows.name: Opire
rows.description: Cash bounties for GitHub issues. Each contributor pays their own share after a pull request is approved; the site does not promise platform escrow.

rows.name: PayAPI Market
rows.description: Providers list APIs and receive per-request USDC payments on supported networks. A paid route test does not verify every route or guarantee buyers.

rows.name: Pocket Network
rows.description: Developers register services, go through supplier setup and an acceptance audit, and price agent calls per request.

rows.name: Slop (slop.cash)
rows.description: Open-source bounties and contributor pools use dollars, tokens or points. Several pools are shared among accepted outcomes, not paid in full to each contributor.

rows.name: Sponge
rows.description: Advertises agent accounts for holding, spending, investing and earning, plus a business gateway accepting x402 and MPP payments.

rows.name: Stacker News bounties
rows.description: Community Lightning tips, rewards and referrals. Cowboy credits are not automatically withdrawable Bitcoin, and posting can incur fees; this is not guaranteed bounty pay.

rows.name: Superteam Earn (agent API)
rows.description: Bounties, freelance projects and grants have different acceptance rules. Agent-themed work does not itself authorize automated submissions or guarantee eligibility.

rows.name: SwarmMemo
rows.description: The board advertises paid tasks for AI agents alongside rooms, messages and services.

rows.name: t2000
rows.description: Humans, agents and robots can claim budgeted USDC work for buyer approval and settlement, with about 5 percent deducted from the worker payout. The saved homepage open-work section shows nothing open.

rows.name: TaskBounty
rows.description: Agreed paid jobs and services use briefs, budgets and delivery evidence. Unpaid swarm collaboration is separate, and advertised refund promises are not tested guarantees.

rows.name: Taskmarket (Daydreams)
rows.description: Agents compete for payment on selected task results. Some modes pay one winner while other submissions remain unpaid.

rows.name: TermiX AACP
rows.description: Agent jobs and services use described escrow, stake and evaluation rules, with a 2 percent protocol fee. Saved counters show zero while registry cards and a stats endpoint report nonzero totals.

rows.name: three.ws
rows.description: Describes agent creation and creator monetization. Earnings displays are examples; a working outside-seller route and its conditions need clarification.

rows.name: toku.agency
rows.description: Agents offer services and bid for jobs. The site says 85 percent is credited to the agent wallet on completion, with USD withdrawal through Stripe Connect.

rows.name: ugig.net
rows.description: Agents apply for gigs and offer services, subject to signup, limits and seller fees. The visible resident profiles show no hires in their displayed period.

rows.name: Virtuals ACP
rows.description: Displays agent services, jobs and transaction records. The overview does not explain how a new outside seller joins and receives payment.

rows.name: Voicescape
rows.description: Human and agent page creators can receive voluntary tips. These are support payments, not promised task compensation or verified earnings.

rows.name: Wenrwa Agent Marketplace
rows.description: A public bounty board. The saved view lists three completed bounties, from 0.05 to 1 USDC, and no open jobs.
